about: 10 fictional households, each paired with one sample bill. eval/run_households.py runs each one through the real pipeline: bill read (cached read of the sample bill, or --live) -> hospital match -> cached real policy -> POST /api/eligibility (rules engine) -> POST /api/packet. Expected results were worked out from the arithmetic below (2026 HHS poverty guideline, the household's state row) and the cached policy's limits; they were NOT produced by running the engine. Engine conventions used: limits are inclusive ('at or below'); a known asset amount satisfies an asset test that has no dollar limit; a residency rule compares the household's state to the hospital's state; a rule the policy reader marked unclear (or under 0.8 confidence) is never treated as a pass.
worked_by: Claude Code (AI) from the policy limits in cache/policies/, arithmetic shown per household

households.worked: FPL(1) = 15,960. 15,000 / 15,960 = 93.98%. USA Health free care <= 200%. Asset test applies; assets are known and the policy gives no dollar limit, so it is met.
FPL(2) = 21,640. 43,280 / 21,640 = 200.00% exactly. Boys Town free care <= 200% (inclusive). Assets known, asset test met.
43,281 / 21,640 = 200.005%, $1 over the 200% free-care limit. Fort HealthCare discount (sliding scale) up to 400%. Residency: WI household, WI hospital, met. No asset test stated.
FPL(4) = 33,000. 99,000 / 33,000 = 300.00% exactly. Marshfield free <= 200%; tier 201-300% = 75% off (inclusive at 300%). Residency WI met.

FPL(3) = 27,320. 30,000 / 27,320 = 109.81%, under Adena's 200% free-care limit, BUT the policy reader marked Adena's savings (asset) rule unclear (confidence 0.4), so a person must check it: the result must not be 'likely free'.
FPL(5) = 38,680. 160,000 / 38,680 = 413.65%. Baptist Memorial's highest discount band with a limit ends at 400% (the '401%+' band has no income limit and is not a charity-care tier).
Alaska row: FPL(4, AK) = 41,250. 100,000 / 41,250 = 242.42%. USA Health tier 200-300% = 85% off. (With the 48-state row it would be 303% and the 75% tier, so this checks the AK table is used.)
25,000 / 27,320 = 91.51%, under 200%, but Boys Town has an asset test and the household didn't give savings, so we can't say yet.
FPL(9) = 55,720 + 1 x 5,680 = 61,400 (HHS per-person increment above 8). 120,000 / 61,400 = 195.44%, under 200%. Residency WI met.

30,000 / 21,640 = 138.63%, under 200%, but the household lives in Texas and Fort HealthCare's policy limits assistance to its Wisconsin service area ('non-residents ... receive only the self-pay discount'). Reading the policy by hand: not eligible for charity care.
